description: Committee recommends applying for $1.1 million federal tree planting funds.
Project would plant 930 trees and diversify species.
Aims to increase city canopy cover to 15-20% by 2060.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Ford asked about financial impact if federal funding application is not approved.
Taxpayers will incur $61,000 annual operating costs for trees starting 2028.
Diversifying trees reduces risk from Dutch Elm disease and Cotton Ash Psyllid.
Staff confirmed the project would not have a mill rate impact.

description: Saskatoon's community emissions decreased 12% since 2014, missing 2023 target.
Corporate emissions decreased 7%; city saved $900,000 annually from LED streetlights.

chips.text: Staff noted landfill emissions are a legacy issue, difficult to reduce quickly.
Homeowners benefit from energy efficiency retrofits through a loan program.
Overall financial savings from climate initiatives are not yet comprehensively tracked.
Food forest pilots target neighborhoods experiencing high levels of food insecurity.
Landfill gas collection system reduces corporate emissions by 60,000 tons CO2E annually.
Zero emission vehicle plan for city fleet coming early next year.

segments.title: 2023 Climate Action Progress Report Presentation
description: Saskatoon's third climate action progress update since 2019.
Community emissions decreased 12% since 2014, per capita by 27%.
Corporate emissions decreased 7% since 2014, not meeting 40% target.
Report includes progress on LEC plan, adaptation strategy, green pathways.

chips.text: Community emissions decreased by 12% or 480,000 tons of CO2E since 2014
LED bulb switch saves approximately $900,000 per year
New Climate Dashboard will communicate progress on Climate Action by 2025

segments.title: Discussion on Financial Savings and Food Forest Selection
description: Councillor Keller asked about overall estimated savings from initiatives.
Staff stated a comprehensive accounting of savings is not yet available.
Food forest sites were selected based on irrigation, soil, and food insecurity.
Federal funding supports the food forest projects.

chips.text: Overall estimated financial savings from climate initiatives are not yet available
Food forest pilots target neighborhoods experiencing high levels of food insecurity
Natural infrastructure fund provides significant federal funding for food forests

segments.title: Corporate Emissions and Landfill Impact Discussion
description: Mayor Block questioned why corporate emissions struggle compared to community.
Landfill waste contributes 48% of corporate emissions, a legacy issue.
Landfill gas recovery system reduces 60,000 tons of CO2E annually.
Staff will explore ways to highlight corporate progress in messaging.

chips.text: Landfill waste contributes 48% of corporate emissions, a significant legacy source
Mayor Block suggested separating landfill data to better highlight corporate progress
Staff will look at ways to highlight progress and minimize areas outside control in messaging

segments.title: Facility Upgrades, Electric Fleet, and Solar Farm Timelines
description: City has $10 million committed to an energy performance contract for retrofits.
Zero Emissions Transition Plan for transit fleet is coming in January.
Zero Emission Vehicle roadmap for the rest of the fleet is coming early next year.
Dendonald Avenue solar farm construction starts early spring, operational end of 2025.

chips.text: City has $10 million committed to facility energy performance contract for retrofits
Zero Emissions Transition Plan for transit fleet coming to committee in January

segments.title: Federal Carbon Tax Impact on Climate Action
description: City does not receive direct federal carbon tax rebates as a municipality.
Carbon tax results in millions of dollars in additional costs for the city.
Federal grants like the Green and Inclusive Building Fund are available.
Climate action plan model is transparent and adjustable for policy changes.

chips.text: Federal carbon tax results in millions of dollars of additional costs for the city
Impact of potential federal carbon tax removal on city's climate plan is uncertain
City's climate action plan model can adjust for changing federal government policies
